hints: Look at each of the 4 structures and ask yourself, is this something every eukaryotic cell needs, or is it a specialist for only one cell type?
Remember which structure organises the spindle in animal cells but is missing in most higher plant cells, and remember that size differences (like in vacuoles) do not mean absence.
walkthrough:
**Start with what both cells share**

Both animal and plant cells are eukaryotic cells. That means they both have a true nucleus, and inside that nucleus they both need a nucleolus to make ribosomes. So number 3 is in both.

**Check lysosomes and vacuoles**

Both cell types need to digest waste and recycle materials, so both can have lysosomes with hydrolytic enzymes. Both can also have vacuoles bounded by membrane, even though they look very different (large and permanent in plants, small and temporary in animals). So numbers 2 and 4 are in both.

**Spot the odd one out**

Centrioles form the centrosome and organise microtubules during division in animal cells. Most higher plant cells do not have centrioles at all and use other microtubule organising centres instead. So number 1 is animal only, not both.

That leaves 2, 3 and 4 only.

options.A: Incorrect because 1 (centriole) is not found in higher plant cells, and it misses out 2 and 4 which are found in both.
options.B: Incorrect because although 2 and 4 are correct, it wrongly leaves out 3 (nucleolus) which is present in the nucleus of both cell types.
options.C: Correct because lysosome, nucleolus and vacuole are all found in both animal and plant cells, while centriole is not.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes 1 (centriole), which is essentially an animal cell structure and absent from most plant cells.
